title: Buying Guide: The Basics of Boring
summary: Boring uses a single-point or sometimes a dual-head cutting tool to remove material in a manner that’s quite similar to external turning. Learn more.
body_text: Chief among these difficulties is vibration or “chatter," a noisy, harmonic-generated event that leads to poor tool life and unacceptable surface finish. Think of it as the cutting tool bouncing against the workpiece. The most common cause of chatter is an overly long boring bar, although depending on the workpiece requirements, this is often unavoidable. Fortunately, there are some techniques that machinists can use to mitigate chatter, no matter how deep the hole. How much to extend the tool from its holder is a matter of great scientific discussion, one filled with complex formulae that consider tangential cutting force, the bar's modulus of elasticity and moment of inertia, and similarly mind-numbing criteria. And while these calculations might provide valuable insight, a few rules of thumb are probably more expedient. For starters, steel shank boring bars are good up to three times the tool diameter or so (abbreviated as 3 x D), more with soft materials like aluminum and brass. Bars with heavy metal or carbide shanks can extend up to 6 x D without too much difficulty, although minimal stick-out is preferred in any machining application and boring is no exception. Modular tools with internal damping mechanisms—Kennametal calls them vibration-free boring bars —can easily achieve 10 x D or more. Sometimes far more.

title: Vivian Wang Awarded Osborn Elliott Prize
summary: Vivian Wang, a China correspondent for The New York Times, has won the Osborn Elliott Prize for Excellence in Journalism on Asia. The award, given by the Asia Society, recognized a series of stories…
body_text: Vivian, a correspondent who’s produced revelatory coverage, received the award for her coverage of China. Vivian Wang, a China correspondent for The New York Times, has won the Osborn Elliott Prize for Excellence in Journalism on Asia . The award, given by the Asia Society, recognized a series of stories by Vivian that examined the contradictions of everyday existence in China, where ordinary people contend with the pressures of living in a society dominated by technological ambitions and fueled by nationalism. The series included an interactive that documented the state’s sustained effort to suppress the public outcry and activism around a woman who had been found chained to a shed. It also included a story from Shanghai, where a chaotic lockdown during the pandemic continued to cast a shadow over the lives of residents, and a story about the challenges older workers face in trying to get work. The jury chair, Marcus Brauchli, described Vivian’s detailed approach as a “poignant and important counterpoint to the narrative emanating from Beijing of China as the new superpower.” “Vivian’s work in China has been revelatory, showing the world some of the complexity and humanity going on there behind the great-power maneuvers that are dominating the news,” said Douglas Schorzman, the Asia editor for The Times. “She consistently kept up her brave and impactful journalism despite unreasonable pressure from the Chinese authorities.” The award is named for Osborn Elliott, former editor in chief of Newsweek.

title: Teleflex Announces Barrigel™ Rectal Spacer AI Model Now Available within Radformation AutoContouring Software
summary: July 23, 2026 - Barrigel rectal spacer expands contouring capabilities via a contouring structure option within Radformation's AutoContour v2.7 software.
body_text: Barrigel Rectal Spacer Expands Contouring Capabilities Through Radformation Partnership July 23, 2026 – Wayne, Pa. – Teleflex Incorporated (NYSE: TFX), a leading global provider of medical technologies, today announced that its Interventional Urology business’ Barrigel™ rectal spacer is now available as a contouring structure option within Radformation's AutoContour v2.7 software. FDA-cleared in March 2026, the software version enables dosimetrists and physicians to efficiently contour Barrigel spacer during the treatment planning process for prostate radiation therapy.1 The AI model was trained using patient MRI and CT datasets from the Barrigel Pivotal Trial, obtained from 11 different institutions and centrally reviewed for consistent contour quality.1,2 In parallel with Teleflex's long-term strategy to significantly streamline the Teleflex business and narrow focus to the critical care and high-acuity hospital end-markets, the company's Interventional Urology business unit continues to drive clinical value as it prepares for its divestiture in the second half of 2026. “Consistent and efficient contouring are critical components of prostate radiation treatment planning,” said Michelle Svatos, PhD, Director, Scientific Research Strategy and Innovation, Interventional Urology. “Integrating Barrigel rectal spacer into Radformation's AutoContouring platform helps streamline clinician workflows while supporting precise treatment planning based on CT or MRI imaging. This integration is another step forward in our commitment to providing radiation oncology teams with tools that support both procedural efficiency and positive patient outcomes.” Barrigel rectal spacer is the only sculptable spacer, allowing physician-controlled spacing for a safe, symmetric, and stable placement.2-7 By helping reduce radiation exposure to healthy rectal tissue, Barrigel rectal spacer may help patients maintain bowel function, quality of life, and minimize treatment-related rectal side effects.8 Clinical evidence continues to demonstrate the long-term benefits of Barrigel rectal spacer in protecting healthy rectal tissue during prostate radiation therapy.8 In May 2026, three-year data from the Barrigel Pivotal Trial presented at ESTRO 2026 showed that zero patients treated with Barrigel rectal spacer experienced Grade 2 or greater gastrointestinal toxicity, compared with 10 percent in the control arm.⁸ Additionally, patients with greater than 1 cm of apical spacing experienced less decline in bowel quality of life at 36 months, reinforcing the critical role of rectal spacing in preserving long-term bowel function after treatment.⁸ "This collaboration represents another step in making AI-trained contouring more comprehensive and clinically relevant. By incorporating Barrigel rectal spacer into AutoContour, we're helping radiation oncology teams achieve consistent contouring across CT, MR and CBCT while integrating seamlessly into the treatment planning workflow,” said Christine Gnaster, Vice President of Product, Radformation. “It's part of our broader commitment to delivering automation that improves efficiency without changing how clinicians work.” On Dec. 09, 2025, Teleflex announced it has entered into definitive agreements to sell the company’s Acute Care, Interventional Urology and OEM businesses to two buyers, Intersurgical® Ltd with respect to Acute Care and Interventional Urology, and Montagu and Kohlberg with respect to OEM. Barrigel Rectal Spacer Important Safety Information Barrigel rectal spacer is intended to temporarily position the anterior rectal wall away from the prostate during radiotherapy for prostate cancer and, in creating this space, the intent is to reduce the radiation dose delivered to the anterior rectum. It is composed of biodegradable material and maintains space for the entire course of prostate radiotherapy treatment and is intended to be absorbed by the patient’s body over time. It should only be administered by qualified and properly trained physicians with experience in ultrasound guidance and injection techniques in the urogenital/pelvic area. Potential complications include but are not limited to: pain associated with the injection; needle penetration or injection of Barrigel rectal spacer into the bladder, prostate, rectal wall, rectum, urethra, or intravascularly; local inflammatory reactions; infection; urinary retention; rectal mucosal damage, ulcers, necrosis; bleeding; constipation; and rectal urgency. Contraindicated in prostate cancer patients with clinical stage T4 disease. Individual results may vary. Visit barrigel.com . Caution: Federal (USA) law restricts this device to sale by or on the order of a physician. About Interventional Urology The Interventional Urology Business Unit is leading in prostate health by advancing clinical evidence, elevating education, and supporting physicians and patients. Our portfolio includes Barrigel™ rectal spacer for men seeking to reduce rectal side effects associated with prostate cancer radiation therapy, the UroLift™ System for men suffering from BPH symptoms, and Deflux™ injectable gel for children with grades II-V vesicoureteral reflux (VUR). title: GLP-1 and menopause: How Semaglutide is changing midlife weight and symptom management
summary: Discover how GLP-1 medications like semaglutide affect menopause, weight gain, and symptoms such as belly fat, sleep, and mood.
body_text: Hormonal fluctuations as you age can make managing weight more difficult. GLP-1 receptor agonists are a new frontier for women seeking relief from menopause-related weight gain and “menopause belly.” There is a growing conversation online about semaglutide and menopause, and the scientific evidence fueling it. For people undergoing the menopausal transition and struggling with weight loss, GLP-1s could offer a safe, clinically-proven way to improve overall health. Key takeaways The menopausal transition is a completely normal part of aging. During this time, people may notice changes in their bodies, such as weight gain, difficulty losing weight, or insulin resistance. GLP-1 therapy can counter menopause-related metabolic slowdown and unhealthy visceral fat gain. Combining semaglutide with HRT and lifestyle changes delivers greater results for people in all stages of menopause. Using GLP-1 for menopause treatment should always be supervised by a medical provider and individualized to the person. There is no one-size-fits-all approach to weight management during menopause. What is GLP-1 and how does it work? GLP-1 stands for “glucagon-like peptide-1” which is a key hormone that helps the body regulate blood sugar levels, insulin levels, and metabolism. When someone eats, their digestive system processes carbohydrates as glucose (sugar) and moves it into the bloodstream. The GLP-1 hormone alerts the pancreas to release insulin, which helps turn glucose into energy. At the same time, GLP-1s tell the body to slow glucagon release, which raises blood sugar levels. This keeps blood sugar levels in a healthy range. GLP-1 medications , also called GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), are used to help the brain and gut work together to control hunger and metabolism by mimicking the GLP-1 hormone. They slow down digestion and reduce hunger signals, helping people feel full sooner and stay full longer. The use of GLP-1 medications can result in weight loss and better metabolic control. They are used to treat type 2 diabetes or obesity. Some of the most common brand names of GLP-1 medications are: Ozempic Wegovy Zepbound Mounjaro Compounded GLP-1 vs Ozempic While many name-brand GLP-1s have become household names, some people may also be prescribed compounded GLP-1 medications. Compounded GLP-1s are created to mimic the original GLP-1 medications by outsourcing to pharmacies not connected to the manufacturers of those brand-name products. Unlike the brand-name products, these compounds have not been FDA-approved. The ingredients are FDA-approved, but the customized final version of the medication is not. Why are compounded GLP-1s created? Although typically it is illegal to copy a medication when the original product is under patent, compounded medications are legally allowed during an FDA-declared drug shortage. Risks of compounded GLP-1s include: Improper prescriptions Dosing errors Lack of standardization Contamination Misbranding of products The FDA is currently concerned with an increase in cases of unapproved compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide marketed in the U.S., encouraging consumers to be cautious of where they are getting their medications from. GLP-1 and the “Menopause Belly” “Menopause belly” refers to the accumulation of visceral fat linked to estrogen decline during the menopausal transition. Visceral fat is normal and something everyone has, which acts as a layer of protection around the organs. Too much visceral fat can lead to a higher risk of cardiovascular disease. GLP-1 therapy has been proven to significantly reduce visceral fat content in adults. However, studies have also found that GLP-1 therapies can result in the loss of muscle mass . Luckily, there are ways to enhance the results of GLP-1 medication to target visceral fat and support muscle preservation. Pair GLP-1 with resistance training 3x weekly. Maintain high-protein intake to support lean muscle. Monitor bone health to prevent loss with rapid weight reduction. Patients who regularly exercise and maintain a healthy diet throughout treatment and beyond have the best chance of preserving lean body mass while losing fat. Why weight gain is common during menopause The menopausal transition is truly a metabolic transition , as hormonal shifts trigger changes in muscle mass, how the body stores fat, and insulin resistance. A new cardiometabolic baseline is set that has an impact on long-term bone, muscle, and heart health. Midlife women gain an average of 1.5 pounds per year . These are the primary factors of a metabolic slowdown that leads to the “menopause belly”: Metabolism slows with age , which results in the body burning fewer calories at rest than it did in younger age. Muscle mass also decreases with age. Together, these bodily changes, along with hormonal changes, contribute to fat gain around the midsection. Menopause also increases the risk of insulin resistance , which can cause blood sugar levels to rise. This may result in the body storing more fat, particularly visceral fat that surrounds internal organs, which is particularly dangerous. Additionally, many women experience increased stress during midlife due to changes in relationships, work, or health. Chronic stress elevates cortisol levels , which can also promote fat accumulation around the midsection. But weight gain alone isn’t the only reason many end up searching for GLP-1 solutions for menopause belly. For many, the menopausal transition can lead to mood changes, anxiety, trouble sleeping, self-esteem issues, and disruption in quality of life. Treatments for behavioral and dietary health are known to improve the emotional well-being of people experiencing menopause, leading some experts to believe weight loss with GLP-1s could have similar benefits. How GLP-1 medications may help menopause-related weight changes There’s a lot of interest in using GLP-1s for menopause weight loss, but what should individuals expect once they begin treatment? The most common outcomes for GLP-1 users are: Reduced appetite and feeling full or satiated longer Improved blood sugar Weight loss (of 10–20% of body weight) Let’s look at these outcomes in more detail. Reduce “food noise” and suppress hunger cues. Hormonal fluctuations during perimenopause can make weight management particularly challenging because they can affect appetite regulation. When estrogen levels dip, appetites may rise—including cravings for carbs, sweets, and other less healthful foods that contribute to weight gain. Improve blood sugar levels and insulin sensitivity. Midlife muscle loss can affect blood sugar regulation, which can also lead to insulin resistance. When the body doesn’t process glucose efficiently, individuals become susceptible to chronic health conditions like high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes, as well as additional weight gain. Encourage fat loss around the midsection. Muscle loss around the middle typically results in fat replacing it. The muscle in the abdomen is a metabolically active muscle, which contributes to metabolism. So when there’s less muscle, metabolism slows. GLP-1 medications can help offset some of these changes. The effects of midlife weight gain extend far beyond aesthetics, contributing to an increased risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes (T2D), and other metabolic diseases. But with the help of GLP-1 medications such as tirzepatide and semaglutide , recent studies show that patients can reduce their total body weight by 10–20%. Semaglutide and menopause symptoms beyond weight How do GLP-1 and menopause symptoms interact? It turns out, GLP-1 therapy may play a role in broader menopause symptom relief beyond just weight management. For instance: Weight gain and insulin resistance during menopause can exacerbate hot flashes. By managing weight fluctuations and glucose levels, patients may experience less intense hot flashes. Some studies indicate that GLP-1s improve mood and mental health , while others suggest an elevated risk of depression and anxiety . More stable glucose levels can improve fatigue and concentration. Although weight loss can contribute to reduced bone strength , the addition of exercise to a person’s routine can help offset bone loss. Combining GLP-1 therapy with hormone replacement therapy (HRT) Can GLP-1 therapy be combined with hormone replacement therapy (HRT)? Yes! In fact, a new study led by Mayo Clinic found that women who used HRT for menopause, along with tirzepatide, lost around 35% more weight than those taking tirzepatide alone. Additionally, a 2024 study found that for postmenopausal women with overweight or obesity treated with semaglutide, hormone therapy led to improved weight loss . HRT and GLP-1 therapies complement each other for other outcomes, too. For example, people in menopause experience a drop in estrogen levels, which leads to bone density loss. Losing weight can also contribute to weakened bones. But hormone therapy has been found to reduce osteoporosis risk in some patients. Furthermore, supplementing lower estrogen levels helps protect muscles, joints, and ligaments, which in turn helps protect bones. For those going through the menopausal transition, hormonal health and weight management often go hand-in-hand. Finding the right balance of treatment through GLP-1s and HRT can improve metabolic resilience and enhance overall quality of life. For the 20% of the workforce in some phase of the menopause transition , holistic support, such as Carrot’s hormonal healthcare journey, can provide much-needed care. GLP-1 side effects and safety considerations For those considering GLP-1 therapy for menopause, it is always a good idea to look at the benefits and potential risks. Some common side effects of GLP-1 medications include: Nausea and vomiting Diarrhea Constipation Abdominal pain Loss of appetite Headaches Infection Irritation at the injection site Patients on GLP-1 therapies can also experience muscle loss or bone density loss with prolonged use, which can compound some of the natural physical changes that accompany menopause. More severe side effects include pancreatitis, gallbladder issues, and thyroid cancer. The best way to understand the risks of GLP-1s and menopause is to speak with a care provider about health concerns, medical history, and overall goals. For those who are postmenopausal and exploring GLP-1s, talk to a clinician about safe, personalized dosing or GLP-1 microdosing options. GLP-1 isn’t a magic fix. Lifestyle still matters. For anyone interested in GLP-1 therapies for menopause weight loss, it’s important to remember that the medications are not a magic fix. They should be approached with caution and care (and always with the advice of your healthcare provider). To get the best outcomes from GLP-1 medications, it’s best to combine treatment with: A Mediterranean-style diet , which emphasizes eating veggies, fruits, whole grains, and healthy fats. Consistent sleep, which helps manage depression and mood changes, as well as hormonal fluctuations that lead to fatigue . Exercise for menopausal health to improve cardiovascular health, regulate blood sugar, and increase bone density. For anyone seeking treatment for weight loss during the menopausal transition, the goal should not be quick weight loss, but rather a holistic, evidence-based approach that supports a person’s individualized needs. FAQs Who should consider GLP-1 therapy during menopause? The ideal candidates for GLP-1 therapy during menopause are those with obesity, insulin resistance, or persistent weight gain despite healthy habits. Most doctors will recommend that candidates try other weight management approaches first before prescribing GLP-1 therapy. How frequently should I be taking GLP-1 medication? Medication Brand Name Frequency* Dulaglutide Trulicity Once a week Exenatide Byetta Twice a day Exenatide extended-release Bydureon Once a week Liraglutide Victoza Once a day Lixisenatide Adlyxin Once a day Semaglutide injection Ozempic Once a week Semaglutide injection Wegovy Once a week Semaglutide tablets Rybelsus Once a day Tirzepatide Mounjaro Once a week Tirzepatide Zepbound Once a week *Frequency may vary depending on healthcare provider recommendations for individual people. Are GLP-1s still effective during menopause? Studies have shown that GLP-1s are equally effective for weight loss regardless of reproductive stage, with similar outcomes among post-menopausal and pre-menopausal women . For those in perimenopause, undergoing GLP-1 therapy can help them manage health concerns at a younger age before they develop into more serious problems during postmenopause. Are GLP-1s a good first step for menopause weight loss? Most doctors recommend that candidates have already tried other weight management approaches, including dietary changes and increased physical activity. Before getting started, patients will need to undergo baseline testing and approach treatment under clinical supervision. Is it normal for midlife women to gain weight during menopause? Midlife women gain an average of 1.5 pounds per year. While this is a normal part of aging, weight gain during menopause can negatively affect quality of life by contributing to insulin resistance, trouble sleeping, dangerous fat accumulation, and mood changes. GLP-1s can help people in menopause manage their weight more effectively Can GLP-1s be used with menopause hormone replacement therapy? Yes! In fact, studies have found that combining HRT and GLP-1s results in 35% more weight loss. For those going through the menopausal transition, hormonal health and weight management often go hand-in-hand. Finding the right balance of treatment through GLP-1s and HRT can improve metabolic resilience and enhance overall quality of life. What is menopause belly? Menopause belly usually refers to the accumulation of visceral fat due to the decline of estrogen production during menopause. Visceral fat is normal and something everyone has, which acts as a layer of protection around the organs. However, too much visceral fat can lead to a higher risk of cardiovascular disease. So while weight gain during menopause is completely normal, it’s important to exercise and maintain a healthy diet to manage dangerous visceral fat accumulation.

body_text: Meet Maximo. The world’s first AI-enabled solar robot Maximo deploys solar panels in half the time at half the cost . Maximo is a true partner to solar construction crews, using artificial intelligence to automate the heavy lifting of solar panels and accelerate solar installation . FAQs What makes Maximo different from other solar robots on the market? Maximo is the only construction automation solution that provides the full end-to-end mechanical installation of solar modules directly in the field. The solar robot results in faster installation and creates safer working conditions, as construction teams do not need to lift heavy commercial solar panels – nor bend to place them – therefore reducing the risk of injury. Maximo is technology agnostic to adapt to any solar module, and quickly expanding to a wide range of clamps, rails and trackers, which enables Maximo to install solar projects with single-axis trackers. Maximo tracks solar installation data, giving EPCs full visibility into their site's construction status. How fast is Maximo? Maximo works with solar construction teams to automate construction projects and install modules twice as fast as standard mechanical installation processes. Has Maximo been tested in real conditions? Maximo has been extensively tested and validated in a variety of conditions and job sites to ensure that it can perform in almost any weather condition, lighting condition, or terrain type. It has successfully deployed nearly 10 megawatts of solar modules to date. Are Maximo’s materials designed to withstand outdoor environments? Yes, Maximo was built to sustainably operate in uncontrolled outdoor conditions. What is Maximo’s power source? Maximo runs on a mobile microgrid, using lithium-ion iron phosphate batteries as a power source. AC / DC inverters and phase converters supply the three-phase electric power required to run the larger components. Is Maximo prepared to overcome problems in the field? Maximo is equipped with a variety of controls and safety measures that allow it to work reliably in the field. The solar robot’s AI-enabled computer vision system detects any inconsistencies in the installation process and self-corrects to minimize any interruptions. The Maximo User Interface enables the operator to monitor the status of the Maximo unit, including the vision system and battery charge state. How does the computer vision system work? Does it have sensors to calculate distances? Maximo combines a series of sensors, cameras, and advanced computer vision and artificial intelligence / neural network algorithms to identify the tracker structure, modules and other surroundings at solar construction projects, which serve as reference for the next module to be installed. Has this kind of technology been successful in other backgrounds and industries? Advancements in computer vision, artificial intelligence and robotics have made it possible to automate tasks which just a few years ago would have been impossible to execute efficiently and cost-effectively. Applications of these advancements have been successful and are being increasingly adopted in other industries such as electronics, agriculture and automotives. In the solar industry, AI technology has been used to automate processes like preventative maintenance and module cleaning. How is Maximo’s panel box replenished? Solar panel boxes can be replenished with most skid steers or telehandlers, which easily lift a pallet of modules and load it into the module storage space through Maximo’s back panel. How does Maximo move within solar installation sites? Maximo is assisted by a human operator to move between rows on a solar construction site, and a skid steer driver tows the robot. What are the optimal use cases for Maximo? While we envision Maximo to have widespread use in every type of solar construction project that uses trackers , this system has great potential to solve problems in extreme desert conditions where working conditions are the hardest and where (in the US) installation jobs are harder to fill. We also see a major benefit for solar module construction teams installing modules on the tallest trackers. Safety hazards surrounding working at heights lead to slower production rates. Maximo allows crews to install safely from the ground at the click of a button. What is the preparation work for implementing Maximo? Site preparation : Staging and site preparation work are nearly identical to site prep and staging for traditional installation. Maximo-specific preparation : Maximo is mechanically calibrated to ensure that its onboard systems are adjusted for the appropriate solar module and hardware used on the job site. How many people are required for Maximo’s operation? Maximo can be run by installation crews of two people. One person drives the system, and the other runs the machine and ensures everything is in place as the robot installs each row. Is Maximo designed for robustness against site variability (i.e., slopes, wetlands)? Maximo’s core robotics technology allows for the system to be positioned in a wide array of orientations and place each panel in the appropriate position. The system has tracks that enable it to maneuver on a variety of ground conditions, including in sandy, muddy, and bumpy environments. How closely does Maximo work with hardware and tracker manufacturers? Maximo works within the supply chain that exists today. We continue to work with module and tracker OEMs to integrate the latest technology as it is released. It is technology agnostic, adaptable to any solar module and quickly expanding to a wide range of clamps, rails and trackers. The Maximo team collaborates closely with tracker manufacturers to ensure seamless operations on current product offerings and to stay ahead of hardware revisions.

title: Sensata Technologies Board Approves Q3 2026 Dividend of $0.12 per share
summary: Sensata Technologies (NYSE: ST) today announced that its Board of Directors approved a quarterly dividend in the amount of $0.12 per share.
